The church is incorporated under Oklahoma law in 1911, with Victor Griffin's help.

column3: The Native American Church originates in the Oklahoma Territory (1890–1907) after peyote is introduced to the southern Great Plains from Mexico.
The church is incorporated under Oklahoma law (1911), and a charter dates from 1913.
The Native American Church is officially created (1918); the Half-Moon way is introduced by James Seymour in 1914 or 1924.
The Controlled Substances Act (1970) prohibits peyote; the American Indian Religious Freedom Act (1978) and the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (1993) later protect its religious use.
Today the church has an estimated 300,000 adherents in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
